chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Wahib ibn Hafas, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: People will continue to decrease until it is no longer said: 'Allah'. When that happens, the leader of religion will rise up, and Allah will send a group from its extremities, coming like a sudden rush like the rush of autumn. By Allah, I know them, I know their names, their tribes, and the name of their commander (and the resting places of their mounts), and they are a group whom Allah carries however He wills; from one tribe He takes one man, from another two... until it reaches nine, so they gather from the horizons three hundred and thirteen (men), the number of the people of Badr, which is the word of Allah: 'Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together; indeed Allah is over all things competent.' So much so that a man might be in his tent, and his tent is not untied until Allah brings him there.

key_terms.أَهۡلِ بَدۡرٍ: The people of Badr (referring to the 313 companions of the Prophet at the Battle of Badr)
key_terms.حُبۡوَتُهُۥ: His tent/enclosure (specifically the tying of it)
key_terms.قَزَعًا: A sudden, rapid gathering or rush
key_terms.يَحۡتَبِي: To be in a tent or enclosure
key_terms.يَعۡسُوبُ ٱلدِّينِ: Leader of religion (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the number 313 in Shia eschatology and how does it relate to the Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* elaborates on the eschatological state of the Muslim community, where faith diminishes until a remnant remains, preceding the appearance of the Mahdi. It specifically links the gathering of 313 companions to the Battle of Badr, emphasizing divine power to transport individuals instantly from their dwellings, thereby fulfilling the Quranic promise of Allah’s ability to assemble people from any location.
